title: Pricing by hours per project for carpet and upholstery cleaning
audience: Owners and crew leads of carpet and upholstery cleaning businesses who quote per job and need a price that covers equipment, consumables, wastewater and margin.
learningOutcomes: Calculate a cost per productive hour from the owner's own figures
Estimate project hours, including set-up, travel and checking time
Build a quote from hours, a rate and a margin, and state its basis and exclusions

instruction.heading: Why hours are the starting unit for carpet work
instruction.body: Carpet and upholstery work is mostly time: the crew on site, the set-up and pre-treatment, the extraction passes, the dry time you must plan for and the check. Start from hours, so that each quote shows its cost, its margin and the effect of adding an item. Per-room and per-item directory prices are references (Yellow Pages, 9 January 2025), not your costs.

instruction.heading: Build the cost per productive hour
instruction.body: Divide the year's total business costs by chargeable hours. Include wages with on-costs where you employ staff, plus vehicle running costs, machine and equipment costs, cleaning solution, water, waste disposal, insurance and admin. Business.gov.au says on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure (1 October 2026). Xero Australia advises dividing by billable hours (3 September 2026). Equipment and solution costs were not sourced for carpet work, so use your own invoices.

instruction.heading: Estimate the hours for each room and item
instruction.body: Time each room and each upholstery item at a standard speed from your own jobs, and record the times. Add set-up, pre-treatment, pack-down, travel and checking as named lines. Add a set allowance for stains or heavy soiling that you find on arrival, and say in the quote that the allowance applies only if the condition is found. Xero Australia suggests 10 to 20 per cent for unexpected work, which is its own range and not a carpet benchmark.

instruction.heading: Turn hours into a price and compare with the directory
instruction.body: Multiply the crew hours by the cost per productive hour, then add a margin for the risk in the job. Compare the result with the directory: four rooms at the top of the steam range is $180 and two dining chairs cost $30 to $60 (Yellow Pages). If your cost-based price is higher, show what the directory price does not include, such as a longer dry time or heavier soiling. Do not cut the cost to meet the directory.

instruction.heading: Keep the quote honest and price extras in writing
instruction.body: State the rooms and items, the method, the hours basis, the exclusions, what the client must provide (furniture moved, pets secured, access), the dry time and the validity. Business Queensland suggests charging additional costs at cost plus a stated percentage, which it suggests as 15 per cent (16 November 2022). Price any extra in writing before doing it.

procedure: Gather the year's total costs and chargeable hours for the same period, with a source for each figure.
Divide total costs by chargeable hours and date the cost per productive hour.
Time each room and upholstery item at a standard speed, and record the times.
Add set-up, pre-treatment, pack-down, travel and checking as named lines.
Multiply crew hours by the cost per productive hour, add the margin, and compare with the directory ranges.
Write the quote with method, hours basis, exclusions, client inputs, dry time and validity.
Record actual hours after each job and review the variance monthly.

workedExamples.situation: [ILLUSTRATIVE] A solo cleaner quotes a steam clean of four rooms and two dining chairs in a three-bedroom home. Estimate: 0.5 hours per room (2.0 hours), 0.25 hours per chair (0.5 hours), 0.5 hours set-up and pack-down, 0.5 hours travel and 0.25 hours checking, which is 3.75 crew-hours. Cost per productive hour is $55 (illustrative; equipment and solution costs are not sourced). Target margin is 25 per cent of price (illustrative).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the cost and the price, and how does the price compare with the directory range for the same scope?
workedExamples.reasoning: The cost is 3.75 x $55, which is $206.25 (illustrative). A 25 per cent margin on price means the price is the cost divided by 0.75, which is $275.00 (CALC). The directory range for the same scope is about $210 to $240 (Yellow Pages, 9 January 2025, vendor; CALC). The cost-based price is higher, so the cleaner shows what the directory range leaves out, such as the longer hours and the solution and water costs, and checks that the 30 minutes per room is realistic. Floor check: at the award Level 1 adult minimum of $25.85 an hour with 25 per cent casual loading, which is $32.31 an hour (Fair Work Commission; 1 July 2025 variation), 3.75 hours is $121.16 before on-costs. That is a floor and not a cost per hour.

equipmentAndPpe: Time log for each job, with estimated and actual columns
Measuring tape or laser measure for area estimates

commonErrors.error: Pricing from the hourly wage alone.
commonErrors.prevention: Include on-costs, machine costs, solution, water, waste, vehicle, insurance and admin.

commonErrors.error: Leaving out pre-treatment, set-up or dry-time planning.
commonErrors.prevention: Add these as named lines on every quote.

commonErrors.error: Copying a directory range as your price.
commonErrors.prevention: Compare the range with your own cost-based price, and say what the range leaves out.

commonErrors.error: Quoting with no method, exclusions or extra-work terms.
commonErrors.prevention: State the method, the exclusions and how extra work is priced before it is done.

commonErrors.error: Never comparing estimated and actual times.
commonErrors.prevention: Record actual times for each room and item, and review the variance monthly.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Pricing guidance only. The Australian Consumer Law applies to price statements, and the ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited (ACCC, 15 July 2026). State rules differ, so check your state's fair trading rules.

Where you employ cleaners, the Cleaning Services Award (MA000022) may set their minimum rates. The Level 1 adult minimum was $25.85 an hour, with a 25 per cent casual loading, from 1 July 2025. The 2026-27 rates were not checked.

Keep a safety data sheet for each cleaning product, keep the original labels, use the PPE the SDS specifies and follow the label (Comcare). The Comcare page covers bathroom products, so carpet-specific solution and wastewater rules are a gap.

qualityStandard: Each quote shows scope, hours or price basis, exclusions, client inputs and validity.
The cost per productive hour is calculated from the owner's own records and dated.
Actual hours are recorded for at least the first ten jobs of each type and compared with the estimate.
No quote is issued without a margin decision and a minimum-charge check.
documentationEvidence: Cost per productive hour worksheet, dated, with the source of each figure
Quote showing scope, hours basis, exclusions and validity
Job time log with estimated and actual hours
summary: Start every carpet quote from timed work and a cost per chargeable hour.
Name the pre-treatment, set-up, travel, checking and dry time, and state the method and exclusions.
Gaps: equipment and solution costs, wastewater rules and 2026-27 award rates were not sourced. The directory ranges are references only.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which costs belong in the cost per productive hour for a carpet crew?
options: Only the hourly wage of the lowest-paid worker
Wages with on-costs, vehicle, machine, solution, water, waste, insurance and admin, divided by chargeable hours
The price the client pays, plus any deposit taken
The per-room price in a directory article

knowledgeChecks.question: A carpet job is estimated at 4 crew-hours and takes 5.5. What should you do?
options: Record the actual hours, find the cause, and adjust the estimate and future quotes
Leave the estimate, because the client has paid
Cut the crew's breaks on the next job
Charge more to this client only and change nothing else

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does a carpet quote need its method and exclusions stated?
options: To show what the price covers, so extra items and methods can be priced and disputes reduced
To make the quote longer for the client
To hide the margin from the client
To lower the client's expectations of the result

sourceReferences: business.gov.au, 'Choose a pricing strategy', https://business.gov.au/products-and-services/choose-a-pricing-strategy, page metadata dated 1 October 2026. Supports: on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure.

Xero Australia, 'How to price services', https://www.xero.com/au/guides/how-to-price-services/, dated 3 September 2026. Supports: divide by billable hours, not total hours; add a set allowance for delays; the guide's 10 to 20 per cent range for unexpected work is the source's own figure.

Jobber Academy, 'How Much to Charge for House Cleaning', https://getjobber.com/academy/cleaning/how-much-to-charge-for-house-cleaning/, 31 March 2026 (first published June 2023). US-leaning source. Supports: cleaners often undercount on-costs such as payroll tax, workers' compensation and unpaid travel, which the source puts at 25 to 40 per cent of wages; a profit factor on cost; annual price reviews; a flat or minimum-hours charge for short cleaning jobs.

Yellow Pages Australia, 'Carpet cleaning costs', https://www.yellowpages.com.au/articles/home-cleaning/carpet-cleaning-costs, published 9 January 2025, updated November 2025. Vendor directory. Supports: per-room, whole-home and upholstery price ranges, and a warning that offers as low as $10 a room may be a basic one-step process.

Fair Work Commission, Cleaning Services Award (MA000022), https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000022.html, variation effective 1 July 2025. Supports: Level 1 adult minimum hourly rate of $25.85 and a 25 per cent casual loading. The 1 July 2026 position was not checked.

Comcare, 'Bathroom cleaning products', https://www.comcare.gov.au/office-safety-tool/spaces/bathrooms/bathroom-cleaning-products, no date shown. Supports: obtain the safety data sheet (SDS) for each product, keep original labels, use the PPE the SDS specifies, and follow label directions. The page covers bathroom products only.

Business Queensland, 'Preparing a business quote: tips', https://www.business.qld.gov.au/running-business/marketing-sales/sales/preparing-quote/tips, last updated 16 November 2022. Queensland. Supports: list add-ons and alternatives on the quote; charge extra costs at cost plus a stated percentage (the source suggests 15 per cent, which is not a benchmark); follow up 7 to 14 days after the quote; confirm scope, capacity and deadline before quoting.

ACCC, 'Setting prices: what's allowed', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/pricing/setting-prices-whats-allowed, page last modified 15 July 2026. Supports: misleading statements about prices are prohibited.

Notes: $55 an hour, the hours and the 25 per cent margin are illustrative and not sourced. The $210 to $240 directory comparison is CALC on the Yellow Pages ranges. The Jobber cleaning figure is US-leaning. Equipment, solution and wastewater costs are a gap.
